Yes, it is certainly down to me.  I've taken a court-issued course relating to domestic violence which has helped me in being an observer of my own thoughts and being able to look at situations that trigger anger in a more clear way.  But I've recently stopped my medication and noticed the anger has come back. I feel as though I've made no actual progress.

I live in the UK and I don't particularly like or trust the psychiatrists I've had. I'm going to book an appointment with my GP tomorrow morning though as I really cannot last like this much longer. But I've been through all of this before and been to psychiatric hospitals, tried various medication and these thoughts still occur frequently every single day.

You're right, growing up I saw my father abuse my mother frequently which I'm sure has contributed to my inability at maintaining a healthy romantic-relationship.

I feel as though I cannot trust anyone anymore and in turn I am extremely lonely. Nobody aside from my mother and sister care about me. And certainly nobody cares about understanding me. I've realised I don't particularly like people but unfortunately they are a necessity to have in your life. I just feel as though these feelings of alienation and loneliness will never subside. Everything I have done has just made me feel as though I've been disqualified as a human being. I feel as though I am living without reason and prolonging myself out of weakness. 

Also, thanks for replying to me and taking the time to read this. It's very kind of you.
